Object based distributions¶

The object surface has two layers. Distribution accepts any dst::Kind and delegates evaluation and sampling to the complete functional catalog. Dedicated objects such as distr::Normal{mean, stddev} carry strongly named parameters and provide exact family-specific operations. Both layers expose density, distribution, random-draw and cumulant methods, with maximum-likelihood fitting where supported. Each page documents constructors, method contracts and runnable examples. The kind-based functions remain on the family pages.

The Surface¶

Object

What it is

Bernoulli

The object form of the Bernoulli distribution: a single trial with two outcomes, success with probability p and failure otherwise.

Beta

The object form of the beta distribution: a flexible family on a bounded interval, the standard model of proportions and probabilities.

Binomial

The object form of the binomial distribution: the number of successes in a fixed number of independent trials with the same success probability.

Burr

The object form of the Burr (type III) distribution: a flexible heavy-tailed distribution with two shape parameters, with exact cumulants below the tail index.

ChiSquare

The object form of the chi-squared distribution: the distribution of a sum of squared independent standard normal variables.

Distribution

The generic object for every dst::Kind; it delegates evaluation and sampling to the functional catalog and supplies numerical cumulants, cumulant generating functions and maximum-likelihood fitting.

Exponential

The object form of the exponential distribution: the waiting time between independent events that occur at a constant rate.

FDistribution

The object form of the F distribution: the distribution of a ratio of two independent chi-squared variables, each divided by its degrees of freedom.

Gamma

The object form of the gamma distribution: a flexible family on the positive axis, the sum of exponential waiting times and the parent of the chi-squared family.

GaussianMixture

A mixture of normal distributions: a weighted sum of normal densities, fitted by expectation-maximisation. It has only an object form.

Geometric

The object form of the geometric distribution: the number of independent trials needed to obtain the first success.

Gh

The object form of the generalised hyperbolic distribution: a five-parameter family that contains the normal inverse Gaussian, the hyperbolic, the variance-gamma and, in a limit, the Student t.

InverseGaussian

The object form of the inverse Gaussian distribution: the distribution of the first time a Brownian motion with positive drift reaches a fixed level.

Laplace

The object form of the Laplace (double-exponential) distribution: a symmetric peak with exponentially decaying tails, the distribution of the error whose best estimate is the median.

Logistic

The object form of the logistic distribution: a bell-shaped curve slightly heavier-tailed than the normal, whose distribution function is the logistic (sigmoid) function.

Lognormal

The object form of the lognormal distribution: the distribution of a variable whose logarithm is normal, the standard model of multiplicative growth.

Lomax

The object form of the Lomax (Pareto type II) distribution: a power law that starts at zero, with exact cumulants below the tail index.

NegativeBinomial

The object form of the negative binomial distribution: the number of failures before the r-th success, and the standard model of over-dispersed counts.

Nig

The object form of the normal inverse Gaussian distribution: a four-parameter family for skewed, heavy-tailed data.

Normal

The object form of the normal (Gaussian) distribution: the bell curve, determined by its mean and standard deviation.

NormalTrunc

The object form of the truncated normal distribution: a normal distribution restricted to an interval.

Pareto

The object form of the Pareto distribution: the power-law distribution of sizes above a minimum, with exact cumulants below the tail index and an exact fit.

Poisson

The object form of the Poisson distribution: the number of events in a fixed interval when events occur independently at a constant average rate.

Rayleigh

The object form of the Rayleigh distribution: the length of a two-dimensional vector whose components are independent zero-mean normals.

Skellam

The object form of the Skellam distribution: the difference of two independent Poisson counts, a distribution on the integers that can be negative.

StudentT

The object form of the Student t distribution: a bell-shaped curve with heavier tails than the normal, controlled by its degrees of freedom.

Uniform

The object form of the uniform distribution: every value in an interval is equally likely.

Weibull

The object form of the Weibull distribution: the standard model of lifetimes and failure times, with a hazard that can fall, stay constant or rise.

Yule

The object form of the Yule–Simon distribution: a discrete power law with exact cumulants below the tail index.

Zeta

The object form of the zeta (Zipf) distribution: a discrete power law on the positive integers, with exact cumulants below the tail index.
